value: THE UPSTREAM-FREEZE HALF OF claim.law.PL_permutation-pin-freezes-every-function-preceding-it-in-source-order.20260901.v1 IS CONFIRMED; ITS TOOLING-GAP AND 'ESCALATE OR REVERT' HALF IS REFUTED, AND THE COST OF BELIEVING IT WAS AN UNMEASURED PRIZE. CONFIRMED, exactly as that law predicts: editing do_players (source line 1651) so its instruction count moves aborts the build with `ValueError: instruction permutation relocation input hash changed` raised from webfrank.py permute_instruction_atoms, even though the pinned do_exit (line 2580) is untouched. REFUTED: that law states 'NO SUCH TOOL EXISTS in the tree - tools/gdl/ contains only webfrank.py and webfrank_audit.py' and concludes 'the documented remedy is unavailable, so the honest options are to revert, or to escalate to the integrator'. The tool DOES exist, at tools/gdl/composed_census/wf_rederive_pin.py - which is the FULL path AGENTS.md trap 15b already names, and the trap even warns in so many words that a lane once reported it missing after checking only tools/gdl/. The PL lane checked only tools/gdl/, wrote the absence into a law, and consequently recorded its probe D as 'did not build' with NO SCORE AT ALL; a run later that unmeasured probe was still being handed forward as 'the unblocked prize (real 1024, 44 clusters)'. When finally measured through the re-derivation path it turned out to LOSE (real 1024 -> 1057), so the false tooling gap did not merely cost a build, it kept a negative axis alive as a headline deliverable for a whole run. THE PROCEDURE, measured working three times in one session on three different upstream edits: (1) make the upstream edit; (2) `ninja build/GUNE5D/src/game/game/.postprocess/body/<tu>.o` - the raw body is all the tool needs, and the WEBFRANK stage aborting on the stale hash is the guard working, not a failure; (3) run wf_rederive_pin.py; (4) READ THE AUDIT, which is the whole point - all four BODY and REGION hashes must print `(unchanged)`, and only the two relocation hashes may print CHANGED; (5) paste the two relocation hashes into config/GUNE5D/webfrank.json with a surgical text edit; (6) `python configure.py`; (7) full ninja. All three re-derivations here returned function before/after and region before/after byte-identical while only before_relocations_sha256/after_relocations_sha256 moved (d09ab1fa -> 5ccdfe34, -> 2844fce8, -> 87c96f03), and each produced a green `build/GUNE5D/main.dol: OK`. WHY THE HASH MOVES AT ALL, which sharpens trap 15b's screen question: after the run-28 name-bound migration the window's relocation hash binds SYMBOL NAMES, and do_exit's pinned window +0x1f0..+0x248 contains exactly ONE relocation, `+0x16 type=109 addend=0` pointing at an ANONYMOUS POOL entry. Its name tracked the upstream edit across the three probes as @1204, @1202 and @1200. So the operative screen question is not only 'does my edit change the pool population' but 'does it change the pool NUMBER that a pinned window's relocation happens to name' - and note the corollary that this session's three-constant fix commit 9182a748f renumbered plenty of pool entries and did NOT disturb this pin, because none of the entries it moved was the one @12xx slot the window names. AGENTS.md trap 15b's ruling stands as written: the upstream freeze is a re-derivation chore, not a wall. TOOL DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED IN PASSING (commit 76a9018d0): wf_rederive_pin.py crashed with `NameError: name 'names' is not defined` in the per-relocation diagnostic loop, on an undefined variable left behind by the same name-bound migration. The crash landed AFTER the hashes printed but BEFORE the 'BODY HASHES ALL UNCHANGED ... pasting is sound' verdict line, so the tool's actual conclusion was never reachable - a lane running it would see hashes and a traceback and could very reasonably conclude the tool was broken and re-derive the pin by hand. The loop now reports the bound symbol name from window_syms instead of the stale r_info index.
